clue.text: In favour of recycled tin currency

indicators.note: material that is recycled is broken down and made into something new, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: being in favour of something is being for it
the word tin, its letters reordered

explanation.surface: Someone who backs turning old tin cans into coins or money.
explanation.walkthrough: The forint is the national currency of Hungary.
explanation.definitionFit: The forint is the monetary unit used in Hungary, so it is an example of a currency.

clue.text: Herb grown by arrogant cook

indicators.note: to cook something is to work its ingredients into a new form, so these letters get mixed

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A proud chef who insists on growing their own kitchen herbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' reads as a noun, the arrogant chef, but it is a verb telling you to mix the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarragon is an aromatic culinary plant used in French cooking, an example of a herb.

clue.text: Organ certain to turn up under urologist's coat

indicators.note: in a down clue, being under something means being placed after it in the grid
a coat is the outside layer, so only the outermost letters of the word before it are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of urologist

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: certain means sure; it is then turned around

explanation.surface: A medical scene where something is sure to show up beneath a urologist's white coat.
explanation.walkthrough: The urologist suggests the bladder, but the coat is only the shell of the word, its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The uterus, or womb, is a muscular body part in females, so it is an organ.

clue.text: Independent continent lacking a flower

parts.note: independent means free

indicators.note: lacking something means going without it, so the named letter is dropped

parts.note: Asia is a continent
taken as written, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A newly independent landmass that has no flowers growing on it.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the A away from ASIA to get SIA, then add FREE.
explanation.definitionFit: A freesia is a fragrant South African plant grown for its blooms, so it is a flower.

clue.text: Try to meet a supporter of facial hair

parts.note: to have a go is to have a try
taken as written
a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: Attempting to meet a fan of beards and moustaches.
explanation.walkthrough: The supporter is not a fan but the little peg a golfer sets the ball on.
explanation.definitionFit: A goatee is a small pointed beard on the chin, a particular style of facial hair.

clue.text: Church airs broadcast by missionary leader with a personal appeal

indicators.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: CH is the usual abbreviation for church
the word airs, its letters reordered

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of missionary
taken as written

explanation.surface: Hymns broadcast from a church by a magnetic missionary preacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' suggests radio, but here it means scattered.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is a compelling attractiveness or charm that inspires devotion in others, a kind of personal appeal.

clue.text: Old knight in control of brotherhood

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so the first pair goes inside the word for control

parts.note: mastery is command or control
O is a standard abbreviation for old
N is the knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: A veteran knight who has taken command of a religious order.
explanation.walkthrough: O for old and N for knight are slipped together inside MASTERY, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A monastery houses a community of monks, so by extension it can stand for that brotherhood.

clue.text: Doctor taking tea and coffee

parts.note: MO is a medical officer
cha is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: A doctor's break with a cup of tea and a coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: MO stands for Medical Officer, an army doctor; cha (or char) is informal British for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a fine variety of coffee, originally shipped from the Yemeni port of that name.

clue.text: Article missing from two signs leading to book stores

indicators.note: something missing from a set is absent, so one copy of the letter is taken out

parts.note: Libra and Aries are two signs of the zodiac
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A grammatical article absent from two road signs pointing towards shops.
explanation.walkthrough: Join LIBRA and ARIES, then remove one of the two A's that meet in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Libraries are places where books are kept and stored for lending, so they are book stores in a literal sense.

clue.text: Holy person going to biblical vessel's stern

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
Noah's ark

explanation.surface: A saint walking to the back of Noah's ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stern' looks like the rear of the vessel; it is the adjective meaning severe.
explanation.definitionFit: Stark and stern can both describe something severe, harsh or bleak in manner or appearance.

clue.text: Bed allocated to small European

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A short traveller from Europe given a bed for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: The bed is read after the small one, even though it comes first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scot comes from Scotland, which lies in Europe, so a Scot is one example of a European.

clue.text: Inject drug into animals' legs

indicators.note: injecting puts a substance inside a body, so one piece is placed within another
into names the receiving word, the one that surrounds the injected letter

parts.note: stags are male deer
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A vet injecting medicine into the legs of animals.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 'animals'' suggests body parts, but legs is the definition: parts of a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Stages and legs both mean separate sections of a journey, race or tour.

clue.text: Nice ears deformed by growth

indicators.note: something deformed has been twisted out of its proper shape, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Attractive ears spoiled by some kind of lump or tumour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growth' suggests a medical lump; here it simply means getting bigger.
explanation.definitionFit: An increase is a rise in size or amount, the same as growth in the sense of expansion.

clue.text: "Toilet" ode composed by unknown American

indicators.note: composing a piece arranges its parts, so these letters are set in a new order

parts.note: john is slang for a toilet
the word ode, its letters reordered

explanation.surface: A poem in praise of the lavatory written by an anonymous American.
explanation.walkthrough: In the US, John Doe is the name given to an unidentified man.
explanation.definitionFit: John Doe is the placeholder name Americans use for an anonymous or unidentified male person.

clue.text: Twist cables to make a barrier

indicators.note: twisting something bends it out of shape, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as fodder
taken as written, as fodder

explanation.surface: Instructions to wind cables together to build a fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' looks like a link word but its letters are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstacle is something blocking the way or hindering progress, just as a barrier is.

clue.text: Old friend discovers stone

parts.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A long-time friend unearths a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: Opal is an iridescent mineral prized in jewellery, so it is a precious or gem stone.

clue.text: Occupational therapist gets time to visit country seat

parts.note: OT is the usual abbreviation
T is the abbreviation for time
Oman is a country in Arabia

explanation.surface: A therapist finds time to call at a stately home in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country seat' reads as a manor house, but the phrase splits: country is Oman, and seat alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ottoman is a low upholstered piece of furniture without a back, used for sitting on.

clue.text: Topless paramour getting close to loved one is immoderate

indicators.note: a topless word has lost its top, which in a down clue is its first letter

parts.note: a paramour is a lover; its first letter is then removed

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of loved
taken as written

explanation.surface: A semi-naked lover getting close to their beloved, which is going too far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to loved one' looks like one phrase; only loved is cut down, and one stays whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overdone is exaggerated or taken to excess, which is to say immoderate.

clue.text: Quite agitated by state of drink

indicators.note: something agitated is stirred up and shaken, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the word quite, its letters reordered
LA is the postal abbreviation for Louisiana, a US state

explanation.surface: Someone rather upset by the condition their drinking has left them in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' suggests a condition; here it is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Tequila is a Mexican spirit distilled from agave, so it is an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Calculation made by setter with money to invest in property

indicators.note: investing in something puts money into it, so these letters are placed inside the next word

parts.note: an estate is land or property
the setter refers to themself as I
M is an abbreviation for money

explanation.surface: A financial forecast drawn up by someone putting cash into property.
explanation.walkthrough: I and M join and sit inside ESTATE. M for money comes from economics, as in the M1 and M3 money supply measures.
explanation.definitionFit: An estimate is an approximate calculation or judgement of a value, number or quantity.

clue.text: In time to take part in performance that's whole

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time
an act is a performance

explanation.surface: An actor arriving punctually to appear in a complete show.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intact is undamaged and complete, with nothing missing, which is what whole means here.

clue.text: Moving image featuring society's prejudice

indicators.note: something moving changes position, so the letters of the next word shift about
a picture featuring something has it included within, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: the word image, its letters reordered
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: A touching photograph that shows the bias of a whole community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' reads as emotionally touching; it signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageism is discrimination against people because of how old they are, a particular kind of prejudice.

clue.text: Taken to dance holding large ornament

indicators.note: letters taken to dance move about and change places
holding something means having it inside, so one letter sits within the others

parts.note: the word taken, its letters reordered
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone escorted onto the dance floor wearing a big piece of jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken' looks like a verb; it is the fodder for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An anklet is a chain or band worn around the ankle as decoration, so it is a piece of ornament.

clue.text: Supernatural being attending special ceremony

parts.note: SP is an abbreviation for special
a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: A ghostly figure turning up at a solemn religious service.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprite is an elf, fairy or spirit from folklore, a kind of magical otherworldly creature.

clue.text: Hospital has a 26 to accommodate animals with rash

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
taken as written
26 is the answer to that clue, a word for location; a sty is one that houses pigs

explanation.surface: A hospital with a ward full of animals, all of them covered in spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rash' is the adjective meaning reckless, not the skin complaint the hospital suggests. The cross-reference is to the solution of 26 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Hasty and rash both describe acting too quickly without proper thought for the consequences.

clue.text: Excellent meaty fish …

parts.note: hunky means beefy or meaty in build
the dory is a sea fish, as in John Dory

explanation.surface: A fine, substantial fish on the plate.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries the fish into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunky-dory is an informal expression for fine, satisfactory or excellent, as in everything going well.

clue.text: … location for one reported

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we want a word that sounds like the item

parts.note: one, following on from the fish in the previous clue, is a plaice, a flatfish

explanation.surface: Following on, a place found for one of those fish, as it's said.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots tie 'one' to the fish of 25 across, so one means one fish; plaice is a flatfish.
explanation.definitionFit: A place is a particular position or spot, the same as a location.

clue.text: Take turns to brew a Trent ale

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients together, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Brewers in the Midlands taking turns to make a local beer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trent is a river in the English Midlands, home to Burton upon Trent, a famous brewing town.
explanation.definitionFit: To alternate is to do something by turns, first one party and then the other, repeatedly.
